column1: # mapping_set_title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 to ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Schema Mappings

# mapping_set_description: Schema-level mappings between the ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (Information Security Management System) and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 (AI Management System) LinkML schemas. This is the reverse of iso42001-to-iso27001.sssom.tsv. Both standards share the ISO Annex SL high-level structure, so most management-system classes, slots and harmonised enums align exactly or closely. Domain-specific elements (information-security risks vs AI-system risks, Asset vs AISystem) are recorded with skos:closeMatch, skos:relatedMatch or skos:broadMatch.

column10: Identical abstract base providing id/name/description across both schemas
Annex SL Clause 7.5 documented-information abstraction shared verbatim between the two management-system standards
Annex SL Clause 4.1 organisation/context entity; identical structure
Annex SL Clause 4.2 interested-party concept; both include Amd. 1:2024 climate-change requirement slot
Annex SL Clause 5.3 organisational role with responsibilities and authorities
Communication line-item shared across the two MS schemas
Audit finding entity used by InternalAudit; identical structure
Statement of Applicability per Clause 6.1.3 d) (both standards adopt the same construct)
Both are the top-level Annex SL management-system class (AIMS vs ISMS) with parallel sub-aggregations; domain (AI vs information security) differs
Clause 5.2 policy class; structure and slots (policy_statement, policy_objectives_framework, commitment_statements, last/next_policy_review_date, integrated_management_systems) are aligned
Clause 6.2 objective class; identical lifecycle slots, domain differs
Risk entity per Clause 6.1.2; AIRisk specialises with risk_source_category and lifecycle_stage but the core fields are aligned
Clause 8.2 risk-assessment result; both wrap risks_identified, methodology_used, assessment_date
Clause 6.1.2 risk-assessment process definition; identical structure
Clause 6.1.3 risk-treatment plan; aligned slots for treatment_actions, risk_owner_approval, residual_risk_acceptance
Annex A reference-control entity; ISO 27001 Annex A has 93 controls, ISO 42001 Annex A has 38 AI controls
Observed event that may indicate an incident; domain differs (AI system vs information security)
Incident entity; both share immediate_actions, containment_actions, lessons_learned, post_incident_review
ISO 42001-specific AI-system impact assessment (Clause 6.1.4); closest ISO 27001 analogue is a domain-specific risk assessment, but they are not equivalent
Process definition for AI-system impact assessment; related to but distinct from ISMS risk-assessment process
The AI system is the central object protected by ISO 42001; in ISO 27001 the closest analogue is a managed information asset, but Asset is broader
DataResource is a specific AI-system resource type; Asset is the broader ISO 27001 concept
Tooling resource (frameworks, IDEs) is a narrower asset type
Computing resource (training/inference compute) is a narrower asset type
Human resource as an AI-pipeline contributor; only loosely analogous to an ISMS Asset
Suppliers are interested parties in ISO 27001 (Annex A.5.19-5.22); ISO 42001 models them as a dedicated class
Customers are interested parties in ISO 27001; ISO 42001 promotes them to a dedicated class
Generic third-party relationship; in ISO 27001 modelled as an InterestedParty subtype
ISO 42001 Annex A.10 concern-reporting/whistleblowing channel; no exact ISO 27001 equivalent, but reported concerns often surface as nonconformities
Identifier slot shared by all NamedEntity instances
Annex SL Clause 5.1 top management slot
Evidence of leadership commitment per Clause 5.1
Amd. 1:2024 Clause 4.1 climate-change relevance determination (identical addition in both standards)
Integration with other ISO MS standards (Annex SL harmonised approach)
Reference to the MS-specific policy (AI policy vs information security policy)
Clause 6.2 objectives slot (AI objectives vs ISMS objectives)
Reference to the risk-assessment process definition (Clause 6.1.2)
Reference to the risk-treatment process definition (Clause 6.1.3)
Affected scope of an incident (AI systems vs information assets)
Reference to the Statement of Applicability per Clause 6.1.3 d)
Topic-specific policies supporting the main policy
Identical enum of audit types (internal, external, surveillance, certification)
Identical enum of integrated ISO/IEC management-system standards
Clause 6.1.3 risk-treatment-option enum (modify, retain, avoid, share)
Both standards have Annex A control catalogues but with different content (ISO 42001 ~38 AI controls; ISO 27001 ~93 information-security controls); only the structural concept aligns
Incident-category enums; categories differ (AI-specific harms vs malware/phishing/etc.) but the modelling intent is identical
